title: HC Velocity & Tiered Billing Sensitivity (Sandbox)
sheet_rows: Scenario,Month,Headcount Plan,Hires This Month,Contractor FTE,Token Burn (M),Avg Unit Price ($/k tokens),Monthly OpEx ($k),Runway Impact (months),Revenue Sensitivity (%)
assumptions: Average token price baseline = $12.0 per 1k tokens (hosted blended mix)
Token burn figures are monthly forecasted millions (M)
Contractor FTE headcount billed as 0.75 cost of full-time equivalence in OpEx
Runway impact measured relative to current committed cushion (months)
Aggressive hiring increases short-term OpEx by hire ramp and benefits, assumed +10% on monthly OpEx per 10 hires
Price elasticity: rough linear sensitivity used for scenario (-20% -> -20% rev), model to be replaced with logit later
summary: Sandbox sheet exploring headcount hiring velocity vs tiered billing sensitivity. Fast hiring (Aggressive) drives token consumption and OpEx up in near term and reduces unit price via product mix changes but consumes runway unless price uplift or efficiency programs (KV cache / quantization) are enacted. Conservative hiring preserves runway but risks missed GTM capacity in H2. Key lever: small unit price changes have outsized runway effect; contractor conversions are cost-efficient near-term offsets.
key_actions: Run a full unit-econ Monte Carlo (1000 draws) using token burn distribution from product telemetry (owner: Priya)
Prototype aggressive quantization + KV cache config on a 10% traffic shard; measure real-world token reduction and latency impact (owner: Ethan)
Prepare a 30/60/90 hiring freeze contingency playbook that maps to token-usage triggers (owner: Diego)
Model dedicated capacity commit offsets for high-volume customers (finance + sales) and potential price-floor negotiations
notes: This is intentionally messy — meant for iterative team discussion in next Forecast offsite.
Numbers use blended rates and should be reconciled with accounting true-costs before external sharing.
See linked artifacts for related tickets and the early cost-of-goods PR in GitHub.
